title: The Goalkeeper — EN/JA/ZH (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 98bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal English Japanese Chinese language learning trilingual football
lyrics:
[Verse 1 — English]
The goalkeeper is the only player allowed to use their hands
For ninety minutes mostly they stand and watch
Eleven other people have all the feelings

[Verse 2 — 日本語]
ゴールキーパーは待機の専門家だ [The goalkeeper is a specialist in waiting]
誰かの特定の警戒心の中で [In the particular alertness of someone]
いつでも緊急に必要とされるかもしれない [Who might be needed urgently at any moment]
それとも全く必要とされないかもしれない [Or not at all]
しかし両方が同様に起こりうるかのように行動しなければならない [But must act as if both are equally likely]

[Chorus — English]
The goalkeeper says — I am ready, I have been ready since the whistle
The ball will come here eventually
And when it does — I will have the only opinion that matters

[Bridge — 中文]
查斯说 — 守门员的工作是没有事件的专注 [Chas said — the goalkeeper's job is concentration without event]
大多数人在事情发生时能够专注 [Most people can concentrate when things are happening]
守门员在没有事情发生的情况下专注 [The goalkeeper concentrates through the absence of things happening]
这是更难的技能 [That is the harder skill]
没有人在中场休息时谈论它 [And nobody talks about it at half time]

[Verse 3 — English]
When the goalkeeper makes the save the crowd erupts
The goalkeeper understands the silence — the goalkeeper chose this

[Outro — EN/JA/ZH]
The goalkeeper
ゴールキーパー [The goalkeeper]
守门员 [The goalkeeper]
That's my boy
